sandhi.note: ā + a → ā; final m before v becomes anusvāra.

samasa.literal: not going beyond what was desired

morph.note: Absolutive of √दा: before -त्वा the root takes the form दत्- (दत्-त्वा), as in the participle दत्त.
Genitive dual of तद्. With verbs of giving Purāṇic Sanskrit often puts the recipient in the genitive instead of the dative.

mantras.anvaya: इति देवी तयोः यथाभिलषितं वरं दत्त्वा (13.28: … सद्यः अन्तर्हिता बभूव)।
mantras.anvaya_en: An absolutive phrase; the main verb बभूव (with अन्तर्हिता) follows at the start of 13.28.
mantras.lit: Thus having given to the two the boon as desired, the Goddess —
mantras.tr: Having granted each of them the boon he desired, the Goddess
mantras.tr_note: The sentence is completed in the first line of 13.28.

comm.t: Both boons have been given, each exactly as asked (यथाभिलषितम्). The Goddess grants what the worshipper wants, without correcting his request.

words.en: the bull among kṣatriyas, foremost of warriors
words.g: m. nom. sg.; compound (see Samāsa); in apposition to सुरथः

sandhi.type: visarga sandhi (-āḥ before a voiced consonant)
sandhi.note: -āḥ before a voiced sound becomes -ā: the visarga turns to y, which is lost before a consonant.

samasa.sense: the foremost of warriors; ऋषभ ‘bull’ at the end of a compound means ‘the best’
samasa.alt: Also an upamita karmadhāraya, क्षत्रियः ऋषभः इव (‘a warrior like a bull’), the analysis grammarians give for compounds of ‘tiger’, ‘bull’ and the like; the sense ‘chief of warriors’ is the same.

morph.note: अन्तर् + √धा ‘to put between, hide’: past participle अन्तर्हित (धा → हि before -त). अन्तर् behaves like a verbal prefix and is kept on the participle. With बभूव: ‘became hidden’, i.e. vanished.
अभि + √स्तु: after the i of the prefix the s of the root becomes ṣ, and the following t becomes ṭ beside it (ष्टुना ष्टुः, 8.4.41): अभिष्टुत.
Absolutive of √लभ्: bh + t → bdh (the t is voiced and aspirated after the aspirate, and the bh loses its aspiration): लब्ध्वा.

mantras.anvaya: (13.27: इति तयोः यथाभिलषितं वरं दत्त्वा) ताभ्यां भक्त्या अभिष्टुता देवी सद्यः अन्तर्हिता बभूव। एवं देव्याः वरं लब्ध्वा क्षत्रियर्षभः सुरथः (13.29: … सावर्णिः मनुः भविता)।
mantras.anvaya_en: The first line completes the sentence of 13.27 (main verb बभूव with the predicate अन्तर्हिता). The second line begins the closing sentence: an absolutive phrase and the subject, whose verb भविता is in 13.29.
mantras.lit: — became vanished at once, praised with devotion by the two. Thus having received the boon from the Goddess, Suratha, the bull among kṣatriyas —
mantras.tr: vanished at once, as the two praised her with devotion. So Suratha, foremost of warriors, having received the Goddess’s boon,
mantras.tr_note: The participle अभिष्टुता is rendered as a clause (‘as the two praised her’). The second line runs on to 13.29.

comm.t: The Goddess disappears at once, as she did after her promises to the gods (12.33: तत्रैवान्तरधीयत). The last thing the two men do is praise her. The second line turns to the outcome for the king.

Textual note: in the digital source this line and 13.29 are repeated as a further block numbered 30. The chapter’s own colophon counts 29 mantras (uvāca 6, half-ślokas 11, ślokas 12; 700 in all), so the repetition is removed in this edition and the closing bījas are placed after 13.29 (see corrections.json).

n. acc. sg. of जन्मन् (n-stem); object of समासाद्य
सम् + आ + √सद् (causative आसादय- ‘to reach, obtain’) + ल्यप् (absolutive)
m. nom. sg. of सावर्णि (i-stem); predicate with मनुः
√भू (bhvādi, 1P), luṭ (periphrastic future), prathama-puruṣa ekavacana, parasmaipada
m. nom. sg. of मनु (u-stem); predicate nominative

sandhi.note: Final t is voiced to d before the voiced j, and the dental becomes the palatal j beside it: त् + ज → ज्ज.
Visarga after i, before a voiced consonant, is sounded as r.

morph.note: Periphrastic future (luṭ): agent noun भवितृ in the nominative, standing for the third person singular. Pāṇini assigns luṭ to a future not of today — fitting for a birth in an age still to come.
Absolutive of the causative आसादय- (आ + √सद्, ‘to cause to sit near’, i.e. to reach, obtain) with सम्: the -अय- of the causative is dropped before -य.

mantras.anvaya: (एवं देव्याः वरं लब्ध्वा क्षत्रियर्षभः सुरथः, 13.28) सूर्यात् जन्म समासाद्य सावर्णिः मनुः भविता।
mantras.anvaya_en: The end of the sentence begun in 13.28b: a second absolutive (समासाद्य) and the main verb भविता with its predicate सावर्णिः मनुः.
mantras.lit: — having obtained birth from the Sun, will become Sāvarṇi, the Manu.
mantras.tr: will be born of the Sun and become Sāvarṇi, the Manu.
mantras.tr_note: The absolutive समासाद्य is rendered as a coordinate verb (‘will be born … and become’).

comm.t: The last line of the Devī Māhātmya returns to its first subject. Mārkaṇḍeya had promised to tell how Sāvarṇi, son of the Sun, became the eighth Manu (1.2–3); the answer is this story — a king who lost everything, took refuge in the Goddess, and will be born of the Sun as Sāvarṇi.

In the Gita Press pāṭha the mantra is followed by the bījas क्लीं ॐ, which close the recitation and belong to the pāṭha, not to the Purāṇa. The colophon then names the chapter ‘the granting of boons to Suratha and the merchant’ (सुरथवैश्ययोर्वरप्रदानम्) and completes the count of seven hundred.
A modern reading: the text ends not with the Goddess but with a human future. Its last verb is ‘will be’ (भविता) — the story of her power closes as a promise about what a person will become.
